verdicts.why: In The Insidious Six (#14) the Rhino is broken out, joins the Six and they confront Spider-Man, so the stage belongs on #14, not #15.
In The Final Nightmare (#27) Connors leaves the Vulture with Spider-Man's mutation, and the Vulture replaces Mysterio in the reunited Insidious Six in #54.

value.title: Spider-Man (1994)#14
value.text: The Chameleon returns with the Insidious Six.

split.title: Spider-Man (1994)#33
split.text: The Chameleon poses as Spider-Man to help frame Peter.
split.on_a_card_about_b: A spy who can wear any face.

split.title: Spider-Man (1994)#57
split.text: The Chameleon betrays the Kingpin for his stepfather, the Red Skull.
split.on_a_card_about_b: A spy who can wear any face.

verdicts.why: The #14 start is right, but the proposed #33 split still holds the betrayal for the Red Skull, which happens in The Six Fight Again (#57). So the split becomes two stages: the framing at #33, the betrayal at #57.
Hydro-Man kidnaps Mary Jane at Niagara Falls in Part 1 (#59), and Part 2 (#60) shows he is a Miles Warren clone.
In Tablet of Time (#24) the aging Silvermane goes after the Tablet to restore his youth and Spider-Man stops Hammerhead's theft for him. He uses the Tablet and turns into a baby in #25.
In Tombstone (#36) Tombstone uses Randy against Robbie and Spider-Man webs him up for the police. The escape with Richard Fisk is in Guilty (#42).

value.title: Spider-Man (1994)#35
value.text: Landon becomes the Kingpin's chief scientist and turns Alistair into a cyborg.

split.title: Spider-Man (1994)#44
split.text: Landon recreates the super soldier serum that turns Felicia into the Black Cat.
split.on_b_card_about_a: A hero who foils Landon's work.

verdicts.why: The #35 start is right (Landon replaces Alistair and makes him a cyborg). In #44, though, Landon recreates the serum and it is the Kingpin who has Felicia transformed, so the split text is fixed to say that.
In The Price of Heroism (#58) the Red Skull's doomsday device turns his son Kragov into Electro. The Beyonder's-world empire is The Gauntlet of the Red Skull (#62).
In Unclaimed Legacy (#55) police chief Kragov threatens to arrest Peter and Robbie and is shown to be the Red Skull's son. He becomes Electro in #58.
In Secrets of the Six (#56) Omar tells Peter the Warriors' story and Spider-Man has to find them before the Kingpin does. He fights beside them in #57.

value.title: Spider-Man (1994)#3
value.on_b_card_about_a: Harry's father, the head of Oscorp.

split.title: Spider-Man (1994)#11
split.text: When the Hobgoblin kidnaps Harry to strike at Norman, Spider-Man goes after him.
split.on_b_card_about_a: Harry's father, the head of Oscorp.

verdicts.why: The kidnapping is in #11, but the father and son tie is already on screen in Return of the Spider Slayers (#3), where Harry has to call his father and Spider-Man saves Norman 'for Harry's sake'. So the stage starts at #3 and the kidnapping is split out to #11.

value.title: Spider-Man (1994)#64
value.text: A high-tech, armored Spider-Man joins Spider-Man's team.

split.title: Spider-Man (1994)#65
split.text: The armored Spider-Man's cocky streak gets him badly hurt. He is rich and his identity is public, and when Spider-Carnage escapes into his world, Spider-Man goes after him in his place.
split.on_a_card_about_b: A cocky armored Spider-Man from another world.
split.on_b_card_about_a: Leads the team, and goes after Spider-Carnage in Peter's place.

verdicts.why: He joins the team in #64, but the sources only show his wealth and public identity in his own world in #65. Those facts move to the #65 split so the #64 stage reveals nothing from later.
In I Really, Really Hate Clones (#64) the six-armed Spider-Man joins the team and turns into the Man-Spider mid-mission, so the whole stage fits #64.
In #64 an actor dressed as Spider-Man is on the team. In #65 he explains Spider-Man is fiction in his world and Spider-Man meets Stan Lee.
In #64 the Beyonder has Spider-Man lead the Spider-Men against Spider-Carnage, who wants to destroy the multiverse. His escape to the armored Spider-Man's world is #65.
In Farewell, Spider-Man (#65) the living Ben of the armored Spider-Man's world brings out the real Peter, and Spider-Carnage jumps into the portal.
In #64 Scarlet Spider, Spider-Carnage's brother through cloning, joins the Spider-Men against him. The stage belongs on #64, not the bare show title.

value.title: Spider-Man (1994)#64
value.text: The armored Spider-Man fights Spider-Carnage's gang with the Spider-Men.
value.on_a_card_about_b: The evil Peter the Spider-Men hunt.
value.on_b_card_about_a: An armored Spider-Man sent against Spider-Carnage.

split.title: Spider-Man (1994)#65
split.text: Spider-Carnage flees into the armored Spider-Man's world and poses as him.
split.on_a_card_about_b: Flees into Peter's world and poses as him.
split.on_b_card_about_a: A rich Spider-Man whose life Spider-Carnage steals to hide.

verdicts.why: The #64 start and #65 split are right, but the sources only show the armored Spider-Man's wealth in #65, so 'rich' comes off the #64 card line.
In #64 the six-armed Spider-Man joins the assault on Spider-Carnage's gang at the Kingpin's base.
In #64 the Spider-Man with Doctor Octopus's arms joins the assault on Spider-Carnage's gang.
Richard is found guilty at the end of The Man Without Fear (#34). In Guilty (#42) he is in Rooker's Island and his father frames Robbie for him.
In The Hobgoblin, Part 1 (#11) the Hobgoblin fails to kill Fisk, learns he is the Kingpin and goes to work for him. The takeover of the Kingpin's empire is #12.
The Hobgoblin kidnaps Harry from Peter and Harry's flat in #11, and Spider-Man brings him back to Norman in #12.
In #11 Norman refuses to pay the Hobgoblin, who goes to work for the Kingpin and kidnaps Harry. In #12 he demands Oscorp for Harry and attacks the Osborns.
In The Mutant Agenda (#17) Landon has promised the Kingpin an army of super mutants and takes his progress call. The same episode shows his real plan is to destroy all mutants.
In The Black Cat (#44) Landon recreates the serum used on Felicia. He is listed with the Kingpin in Six Forgotten Warriors (#54), where the reunited Six hunt the doomsday device.
In #17 the Hobgoblin threatens to expose Landon's double-cross unless he is paid. The research theft and the accident that mutates Landon are #18.
The Shocker is broken out and joins the Insidious Six in #14. In The Awakening (#47) he and Landon take Morbius, and the Kingpin and Landon study him.
In Tablet of Time (#24) both bosses go after the Tablet and Tombstone kidnaps Vanessa for Silvermane. Alisa's kidnapping and the exchange are #25.
In Venom Returns (#37) Connors introduces Jim Rhodes of Stark Enterprises at Tony's demonstration and War Machine fights Venom. In #38 he is hurt and Tony sends Iron Man.
In #37 Kasady is put in the cell next to Brock at Ravencroft, they dislike each other at once, and he bonds with the symbiote's offspring as Carnage. The fight and the portal are #38.

Felicia does start dating Jason in Rocket Racer (#32), but Jason is not revealed as the Hobgoblin until Goblin War! (#40). A Felicia and Hobgoblin stage at #32, with the card line 'The Hobgoblin's girlfriend', would give away that reveal.
In Framed (#33) Matt tells Peter he lost his father to the Kingpin and suspects him of the framing, and the Kingpin's men fire on Daredevil. Revealing Fisk's identity and facing the Kingpin are #34.

At the end of The Spider Slayer (#2) the Kingpin offers Alistair money for new Spider-Slayers and blames Spider-Man for his father's disappearance. The failed attack and the order to keep working are #3.

value.title: Spider-Man (1994)#2
value.text: Norman Osborn promises Alistair a hoverchair in return for his father's work, and carries him to safety when Oscorp burns.
value.on_a_card_about_b: The son of the inventor Norman hires.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Promises Alistair a hoverchair for his father's work.

split.title: Spider-Man (1994)#3
split.text: Alistair holds Norman responsible for his father's death and sends his Spider-Slayers after him.
split.on_a_card_about_b: Blames Norman for his father's death.
split.on_b_card_about_a: The man Alistair blames for his father's death.

verdicts.why: The #2 facts are right, but there they are on the same side, so 'enemy' is the wrong kind for #2. The proposed #2 card lines were also swapped: Norman's card must describe Alistair, and Alistair's card must describe Norman.
Eddie is already a Bugle reporter chasing the Lizard story in #1. Jameson fires him in #2, rehires him for the shuttle photos in #8, and fires him again in #9.
In Morbius (#19) Michael becomes a vampire and frightens Felicia that night. In #23 she learns he was the creature, he kidnaps her, and he takes the Recombinator blast for her.
In The Awakening (#47) Black Cat holds Whistler's weapon on the freed Morbius but cannot use it. The hunt for Miriam and leaving with him are #48.
The Awakening (#47) synopsis has Black Cat using a weapon Whistler gave her, and the episode's quote is Whistler agreeing to help her.

Arming the Black Cat against Morbius in #47 is not an ally turn, and Whistler had already been planning to take Morbius down with Blade since #22. The ally stage (nursing him, the serum) really starts in The Vampire Queen (#48), so the move to #47 is wrong.
